about.title: Ross Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Ross is a small, quiet Marin County town, but the products people use here — from household appliances to tools, vehicle parts, and outdoor equipment used near Ross Common and the trails off Sir Francis Drake Boulevard — are made and sold the same way they are everywhere else in California. When a product fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the person hurt by it doesn't have to prove the company was negligent. California's strict liability rules generally focus on whether the product was defective and whether that defect caused harm. That's a meaningfully different standard than most personal injury claims, and it can involve manufacturers, distributors, and retailers all at once. If a defective product has hurt you or someone in your family in Ross, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, at no cost to you, to talk through what happened and what options exist. There's no obligation, and no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Ross Residents

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California's strict liability approach generally means you only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that the company was careless. This can simplify what you have to prove compared to a typical injury claim.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product. An attorney can help sort out who was actually responsible for getting the flawed product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the defective product, its packaging, and any related paperwork intact is often critical to proving what went wrong. An independent attorney can advise you on how to safeguard that evidence early.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability claims often run on strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury. This is different from ordinary negligence claims, where you'd need to show carelessness.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Don't repair, discard, or alter it. Preserving the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury is often essential to building a strong claim, so store it somewhere safe until an attorney can review it.

items.question: Ross is a small town — does that affect my claim?
items.answer: Not really. Whether a defective product injured you at home near Ross Common or elsewhere in Marin County, California's product liability rules apply the same way regardless of the size of the town. What matters is the defect and the injury it caused.

items.question: Is there a cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and the attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you.
